issue_context.title: Hikvision integration with self signed certificate
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I am using a hikvision camera with a self signed (internal ca) certificate and cannot get the binary sensors setup. I think there is currently no way to let HA trust an internal CA. Maybe a solution is to implement a new parameter (verify_ssl) to get this working with a self signed certificate or a certificate signed by an internal CA.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.5.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

hikvision

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/hikvision/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
binary_sensor:
  - platform: hikvision
    customize:
      field_detection:
        ignored: true
      line_crossing:
        ignored: true
    host: myhost.mydomain.internal
    password: !secret gang_kamera_password
    port: 443
    ssl: true
    username: !secret gang_kamera_username
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/pyhik/hikvision.py", line 496, in alert_stream
    stream = self.hik_request.get(url, stream=True,
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/requests/sessions.py", line 555, in get
    return self.request('GET', url, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/requests/sessions.py", line 542, in request
    resp = self.send(prep, **send_kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/requests/sessions.py", line 655, in send
    r = adapter.send(request, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/requests/adapters.py", line 514, in send
    raise SSLError(e, request=request)
requests.exceptions.SSLError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='myhost.mydomain.internal', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /ISAPI/Event/notification/alertStream (Caused by SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError(1, '[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1125)')))
```


### Additional information

_No response_

I gave it a try, the following workaround is working:

1. SSH into Home Assistant using Port 22
2. Get a shell for the ha docker container: "docker exec -t -i homeassistant /bin/bash"
3. Copy the trusted ca/public certs to the local store: "cp /ssl/ca.pem /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/"
4. Update the local certificate store: "update-ca-certificates"

Now i am able to use a SSL encrypted connection to the Hikvision camera. 

To make this sustain updates we need to automate this process on every HA restart:

configuration.yaml:
```
shell_command:
  update_ca_store: 'cp /ssl/ca.pem /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/; update-ca-certificates'
```

automation:
```
alias: my_automation
description: ""
trigger:
  - platform: homeassistant
    event: start
condition: []
action:
  - service: shell_command.update_ca_store
    data: {}
mode: single
```

@h4de5 Thanks for your help. At least i can live with this workaround.

We no longer allow integrations to add or change a platform YAML configuration.

More information on this can be found in Architecture Decision Record:

- ADR-0007: <https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/blob/master/adr/0007-integration-config-yaml-structure.md#decision>

Please note that this integration connects to a device or service and another Architecture Decision Record applies that disallows the use of YAML configuration in favor of a configuration flow via the UI:

- ADR-0010: <https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/blob/master/adr/0010-integration-configuration.md#decision>

See our developer documentation on how to get started creating a configuration flow for this integration:

<https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/config_entries_config_flow_handler>

As these changes often involve a bit of work and some significant shift in the current code, we will close this PR for now.

We (and our community!) would really appreciate it if you could start on the refactoring of this integration in a new PR.

Thanks already! :+1:
